title: The Lakshmi who stays
hookLine: Indra lets a sage's garland be trampled and fortune leaves the worlds; the Sri Sukta asks for the Lakshmi who does not go away
carry: Lakshmi stays where she is honored

lines: CHURN THE OCEAN, BRING HER BACK.
cards: A sage hands the king of the gods a garland. Indra, riding his great white elephant, drops it onto the elephant's head, and the elephant flings it to the ground and tramples it.
In the Vishnu Purana, the sage, Durvasa, is furious: because you scorned this, he says, your fortune will leave you. And it does. Sri walks out of the three worlds.
Plants wither. Nothing shines. That's why the gods had to churn the ocean, the story this week began with: to bring her back.

teach.b: When Lakshmi rose again, the Vishnu Purana says, Indra praised her with a hymn and asked for one thing: never leave the three worlds again. She agreed. The Sri Sukta asks the same, in its own words.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO DOES NOT GO AWAY.
teach.b: In paraphrase: bring me, Jatavedas, that Lakshmi who does not go away, in whom I may find gold, cattle, horses and people. One long word: anapagamini, the one who does not go away.
You only ask for someone who stays if you know what it is when someone leaves. Tradition calls Lakshmi restless.

teach.h: SHE STAYS WHERE SHE IS HONORED.
teach.b: Here's the teaching, as many Hindus understand it: Lakshmi stays where she is honored. Indra lost her not by being poor but by treating a gift as nothing. That's why so many Hindu homes treat fortune like a guest.
If a foot touches money or a book, a child is taught to touch it and bring the hand to the forehead, a small sorry.
A first paycheck is often set before the family shrine, or offered to elders, before a rupee or a dollar is spent.
And look at the hymn's list: gold, cattle, horses, and last, people. The faces around the table are counted among the riches.
Today: a paycheck lands Friday and is gone by Thursday. The Sri Sukta doesn't promise more of it. It asks for the fortune with roots, and the story says how she's kept: with respect, not grabbing.
A week behind us: the watcher, the goddess who is Brahman, two who are never apart, the voice in every word, and Lakshmi, rising, invited by fire, asked to stay.

how: The Sri Sukta is chanted by some Hindus in Lakshmi worship at home and in temples, including at Diwali, and some families recite it on Fridays.

o: a hymn about trading cattle and horses for gold
a prayer to win a sudden windfall of gold
a hymn asking Lakshmi to come and never leave

games.q: inside the line — tap the pairs.
p: the sage whose garland Indra scorned
the one who does not go away
the last riches on the list

s: Indra lost Sri by being poor
he lost her by scorning a sage's gift. in the Vishnu Purana, fortune left all three worlds.
after the churning, Indra asked Lakshmi never to leave again
he praised her with a hymn, and she agreed.
the hymn pretends fortune never leaves
it asks for the one who does not go away, which admits that fortune can.

games.q: your first paycheck arrives, and your grandmother says to set it before Lakshmi first. by this week's stories, why?
o: so the goddess can take her cut.
Lakshmi stays where she's honored: thanks first, then spending.
it's bad luck to spend money on a weekday.
games.why: Indra lost Sri by scorning a gift; the Sri Sukta asks for the Lakshmi who does not go away. honoring fortune is how families ask her to stay.

practice: Notice the breath first: it leaves, and it comes back, without being asked.
Then bring to mind one good thing in your life that hasn't gone away, a friend who keeps answering, a kitchen, a song that's still there, and rest with it, letting the thanks be quiet.
If you pray, you can name it before Lakshmi or before God, in the words you already use; if you don't, let the steady thing be enough.

wordCard.voice: The Sri Sukta. The hymn to Sri, called Lakshmi, which asks the fire to bring her, and asks for the one who does not go away.

orig.note: Sanskrit: anapagāminīm, 'the one who does not go away,' Lakshmi in the Sri Sukta.

carryVoice: Your line: Lakshmi stays where she is honored. Back tomorrow, same hill.
